properties.name: Adi Badri
properties.description: The Adi Badri temple complex is a cluster of 16 small shrines. Seven temples of this chain were built during the late Gupta period.

properties.name: Vriddh Badri
properties.description: The Vriddha Badri legend says that Vishnu appeared in the form of a Vriddha or old man before sage Narada who performed penance here.

properties.name: Bhavishya Badri
properties.description: According to the legend, when evil transcends the world, the mountains of Nara and Narayana would block up the route to Badrinath and the sacred shrine would become inaccessible. Then, Badrinath will appear at the Bhavishya Badri temple and be worshipped here.

properties.name: Yogadhyan Badri
properties.description: Yogadhyan Badri, also called Yoga Badri is the same place King Pandu, father of the five Pandavas, meditated  to god Vishnu to cleanse him of the sin of killing of two mating deer, who were ascetics in their previous lives.

properties.name: Dhyan Badri
properties.description: The legend of Dhyan Badri (meditating Badri) is linked to the Urvarishi, son of King Puranjaya of the Pandavas lineage who meditated in the Urgam region and established the temple for Vishnu.

properties.name: Badrinath
properties.description: The Badrinath Temple also known as the Badrinarayan Temple, located in Uttarakhand's Badrinath town, is one of the four important pilgrimages in the state.

properties.name: Narsingh Badri
properties.description: It is believed that one arm of the Narsingh idol is getting emaciated with time and finally fall off. When the arm disappears, the main shrine of Badrinath will be closed to the world and Lord Badrinath will shift to Bhavishya Badri shrine.

properties.name: Ardha Badri
properties.description: Ardha Badri (half Badri), located on the Joshimath-Tapovan road is in a remote village called Mrig and can be approached only by short trek along a steep bridle path.
